title: Anthropic doubled the hardest benchmark in AI and then cut your bill
description:
Anthropic just broke the one rule every winning AI company follows: they made their best model twice as good and then cut your bill.

Claude Fable 5.1 more than doubled its score on Terminal-Bench-Science, from 24.7 percent to 52.6, and pushed the overall terminal benchmark from 42 to 55.8. And instead of a price hike, the base price stayed put while cache reads dropped 75 percent. A typical workload now runs about 25 percent cheaper, and agent-heavy workloads that reuse context save up to 45 percent. Anthropic also says the model refuses far fewer safe coding and medical questions, you can watch its reasoning as it works, and it's live today on Claude, the API, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure.

The honest catch: the discount lives in cache reads, so if your workload doesn't reuse context, your bill barely moves.

And the wildest part: Fable 5.1 has a twin called Claude Mythos 5.1. Same base model, fewer guardrails, locked inside special access programs for cybersecurity and life sciences teams. The most unrestricted Claude ever built is the one you're not allowed to touch.

What's your take? Comment below and follow for more AI news that actually matters.
